releases.name: v0.17.4 — Mission continuity and recovery
releases.body:
# v0.17.4 — Mission continuity and recovery

Native V2 worker reconciliation can use a matching child's persisted idle outcome when the public
event history lacks a terminal event. Active or unproven writers remain reserved; formal validation
and accounting remain separate.

Explicit same-author continuation preserves the current user intent and predecessor evidence without
transferring prior Mission authority. Reviewer independence and active-writer protection remain in
place. Natural-language recognition is pattern-based and does not cover every possible formulation.

Recovery can resume direct planning after a quiescent Coordinator, reconcile failed Reviewer
corrections, and traverse more than 256 settled descendants without releasing active or unknown
writers. Exceptionally large individual native histories or child listings can still be unproven.

The runtime asset marker is `0.17.4-mission-recovery-v1`. Installing a package does not reload an
already-running shared host, and these changes do not establish recovery of a particular real Mission.


SHA-256 (`sortie-dogs-0.17.4.tgz`): `ce0f358fb40bdada356475851f3bbe27130d6d5247eecf5180698412df3be3cb`

# v0.17.3 — Git write-gate and Worker settlement

Scoped Git commits can use the invocation-local `commit.gpgsign=false` setting alongside identity options without relaxing native permissions, index scope checks, or restrictions on other Git configuration and repository overrides. Simple Python display expressions containing quoted data are no longer mistaken for Git write commands; actual Git write protection remains in place.

The V2 host adapter retains the admitted owner of a nested Worker when a native call returns an implicitly backgrounded Job. Foreground settlement retains its terminal output for recovery if accounting fails, and reconciliation keeps the actual terminal and required validation outcome distinct.

The runtime asset marker is `0.17.3-git-worker-settlement-v1`. Installing a package does not change an already-running shared host; restart remains a separate manual operation. These changes do not establish recovery of any particular production Mission.

SHA-256 (`sortie-dogs-0.17.3.tgz`): `c9aacd1cc1482f5a16fa979038b7642a6368e9e92ab4e4e0c194e6ad5c331be7`

# v0.17.2 — Review collector recovery

Review source collection handles inherited non-worktree Git directories as declared filesystem outputs. Git metadata bytes remain fingerprinted while their contents are omitted from automatic Reviewer excerpts and diffs, including in nested repositories.

When an unrelated historical file cannot be read because of permissions, Review reports the uninspected coverage rather than treating its bytes as verified. Current inputs and validation-bound files remain strict, and an unknown coverage gap cannot silently become a low-risk Review skip.

The runtime asset marker is `0.17.2-review-collector-recovery-v1`. Installing a package does not change an already-running shared host; restart remains a separate manual operation. Fixture results do not establish recovery of the original production Mission or an actual model-backed CLI startup.

## Changes
- Recover prelaunch refusals against failed predecessor admissions while preserving active and unknown executions.
- Improve test selection and test-debt workflow for supported validation paths.
- Support credential-free candidate preflight without weakening inference authentication.

The attached fixed archive has SHA-256 `6ecf3d05e1efe0abab94005eca2f442b90514125260aa59f78fd12bd3949d615`. Fixture validation does not establish production recovery or real-world test savings.

# v0.17.0 — Ordinary Mission test optimization and ledger recovery

Test Gate guidance, bounded Test Debt Audit and the managed Full Test Guard/JOIN work through ordinary Missions. Supported runners and boundaries are explicit; arbitrary commands are not universally intercepted. Regression, boundary, API and security coverage remain important.

Goal-ledger history is retained across the prior event limit using bounded paging. At the new bound, status can report an unreconciled read-only diagnostic without treating pending reservations or unknown costs as settled. Existing 0.1/0.2 history is retained. After migration to schema 0.3, use a compatible newer runtime and keep the ledger with its `.blobs`. The exact capacity path behind the reported production screenshot remains unknown.

The existing public V2-hook tests exercise actual Node owner/waiter processes and failure/cancellation boundaries. The two authorized real-Agent trials did not observe Guard/JOIN, and fixture evidence does not replace that observation. An actual saved Mission UI image from the earlier candidate was reviewed independently; it does not show the current candidate or prove Guard activation. No general speedup is claimed.

- Main commit: `9964f74cd912505f28c6258f359fd40e067857e3`
- Fixed archive SHA-256: `4705c74ebccec6842ef3a4dee5c68c7e6337ab00ac09bd61c1703cd6ea1bd8e7`
- Runtime marker: `0.17.0-test-optimization-v1`

GitHub distribution, npm publication, installed files and the running shared host's loaded version are separate states. The shared host has not been restarted.
